structure.title: 2021 - 2024 Sustainability Strategy
structure.heading: 4.3 2021 - 2024 Sustainability Strategy
structure.summary:
- CEO message highlights a landmark year (2024) concluding CGD’s 2021–2024 sustainability cycle, with record financial results and full repayment to the State of the 2017 recapitalization plan.
- Strong integration of sustainability into operations and culture, positioning CGD as a leader in sustainable financing in Portugal.
- Delivery of the 2021–2024 Sustainability Strategy: 231 actions with 96% completed, advancing a low‑carbon economy and projects with positive social and environmental impact aligned to the UN SDGs.
- Key ESG advancements: 2050 Carbon Neutrality Transition Plan, enhancement of the ESG Rating Model, and issuance of three sustainable debts to embed sustainability in business and risk processes.
- Regulatory alignment and reporting: adoption of CSRD ahead of requirements; alignment with EBA, ECB, and Bank of Portugal expectations on climate and environmental risk; performance in MSCI, CDP, and Sustainalytics tied to variable remuneration.
- People and culture: €3.7 million invested in training and development (+26% YoY); internal merit and excellence awards (eight editions, 337 employees recognized); rollout of an Equality Plan to drive Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion.
- Social impact: approximately €19 million invested in education, culture, and social support, benefiting the third sector and vulnerable groups.
- Group engagement: first Caixa Group Sustainability Week in 2024 with participation from eight international entities, strengthening a group-wide sustainability culture.
- 2021–2024 Sustainability Strategy pillars:
  1) Sustainable and Inclusive Financing
  2) Climate Risk Management
  3) Equity, Digital, and Financial Inclusion
  4) Transparent Governance Models
  5) Disclosure of Sustainability Information
- Strategy outcomes included new sustainable products, climate transition plans, staff capacity building, and strengthened ESG policies; five targets set and monitored annually across the five pillars.
- Investment plan: €241 million in 2024 (including ~€78 million for the new head office deed), focused on competitiveness, solidity, and efficiency; ~€65 million directed to digital innovation (apps, remote operations, online contracting, open banking) to sustain leadership in digital banking and enhance customer journeys.
- Materiality: a 2021 analysis engaging nine stakeholder groups identified nine material topics, each mapped to key SDGs and targets to guide disclosures and actions.
- Forward-looking commitment: despite potential regulatory slowdowns, CGD reaffirms dedication to sustainable development and responsible business practices in the 2025–2028 strategic cycle, embedding sustainability across all entities and governance for lasting positive societal and environmental impact.

nodes.title: Material Topics and Main Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) Impacted.
nodes.heading: 4.3.1 Material Topics and Main Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) Impacted.
nodes.start_phrase: To support the development of the Sustainability Strategy, a materiality analysis was conducted in 2021 based on a dialogue process with nine stakeholder groups, which allowed for understanding their expectations and concerns regarding Caixa's ESG performance.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines a 2021 materiality analysis based on dialogue with nine stakeholder groups, identifying nine ESG topics relevant to Caixa’s internal and external stakeholders.
- Maps each material topic to the most relevant Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and targets.
- Positions the SDGs as a core framework guiding Caixa’s strategy, with defined quantitative and qualitative goals to focus impact where the bank can contribute most.
- Describes implementation of the Sustainability Strategy through a bank-wide, dynamic action plan aligned with the 2021–2024 Strategic Plan, comprising 37 macro-initiatives and 231 actions.
- Highlights progress under the “Sustainable and Inclusive Funding” pillar, noting completion of key initiatives: creating an ESG-responsible financial product framework; issuing Green/Social/Sustainability-linked bonds; advising clients on sustainable debt; developing ESG products and financing lines aligned with the EU Taxonomy; establishing a Caixa-specific green/brown activity framework aligned with the Taxonomy; and integrating ESG performance analysis across all assets under management.

nodes.title: Implementing the Sustainability Strategy
nodes.heading: 4.3.2 Implementing the Sustainability Strategy
nodes.start_phrase: In this context, and to achieve this, Caixa has implemented a dynamic action plan that cuts across all areas of the Bank, with the aim of executing the 2021 - 2024 Strategic Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Overview and alignment: Caixa uses the UN Sustainable Development Goals as the strategic compass for its sustainability agenda, setting quantitative and qualitative targets to maximize impact.

- Strategy execution (2021–2024): A cross-bank action plan with 37 macro-initiatives and 231 actions reached a 96% overall completion rate in the final year of the cycle.

- Pillars and progress
  - Sustainable and Inclusive Funding (100%): Full delivery of ESG-aligned products, green/social/sustainability-linked bond frameworks and issuances, taxonomy-aligned product development, ESG integration in assets under management, and a Sustainable Financing Policy.
  - Climate Risk Management (89%): Strong progress with remaining actions focused on supplier ESG integration, biodiversity/offset collaborations, and financed emissions targets for priority sectors; carbon neutrality transition rollout ongoing.
  - Equality, Diversity, and Financial/Digital Inclusion (94%): Broad delivery on inclusion, gender equality, community support; pending items include full dematerialization of asset subscriptions, expanded health and well-being programs, and rollout of ESG e-learning.
  - Governance Models (100%): Policies, governance structures, leadership balance, and engagement practices fully established, including a climate and environmental risk policy and asset manager engagement policy.
  - Sustainability Information Disclosure (100%): Best-practice reporting, ESG ratings engagement, stakeholder materiality, double materiality adoption, and responsible ESG communication fully implemented.

- Key achievements by pillar
  - Sustainable finance:
    - First Sustainable Finance Framework (aligned with ICMA Green/Social/Sustainability principles).
    - ESG bond issuances: €500m senior preferred for green/social objectives; two green bonds totaling €800m for energy-efficient residential mortgages.
    - Dedicated financing lines for ESG upgrades, decarbonization, circular economy, EV/hybrid leasing, and InvestEU green investments.
    - Asset management: deeper ESG integration; multi-asset SRI fund reclassified to SFDR Article 9; recognition in The Banker’s Sustainable Banking Revenues 2023 (63rd globally, 5th Iberia).
  - Climate risk:
    - First Portuguese bank (2021) with an ESG rating model for clients across sectors.
    - Carbon Neutrality and Climate Risk Management Transition Plan with 2030 GHG targets and client engagement for portfolio alignment.
    - ISO 14001 Environmental Management System certification maintained at HQ.
    - Full implementation of ECB climate/environmental risk expectations, including a comprehensive external context scan feeding materiality.
    - Strong performance in ECB climate risk stress test and EU-wide EBA stress test (2023): CET1 at 17.97% in adverse scenario; 3rd lowest capital depletion among 70 banks, 1st among ECB-supervised peers.
  - Inclusion and community:
    - Caixa Social Awards (3 editions): 106 projects, >€2.2m funding; first social impact report for the 5th edition (2023).
    - Caixa Mais Mundo scholarships (4 editions): 1,130 students, €1.35m.
    - Volunteering and donations: 16,000+ furniture items and 1,565 IT devices donated.
    - “Sou Cidadão” program: 298 identity documents issued for homeless individuals to enable access to services.
    - Equality Plan launched; talent programs (High Flyers, Top Performers); broad ESG e-learning (climate risks, DEI, sustainable finance).
  - Governance:
    - 15 Sustainability Committee meetings over the cycle; refreshed Corporate Sustainability Policy and group ESG expansion plan.
    - Corporate Climate Risk Management Policy published; remuneration policies for governing bodies and employees updated to embed ESG criteria.
  - Disclosure and ratings:
    - Allocation and Impact Reports for sustainable debt (2021, 2023, 2024).
    - TCFD-aligned reporting.
    - ESG ratings and recognitions: Sustainalytics improved from 21.3 (2021) to 13.4 (2025, low risk; top 10% of banks); CDP Climate Change 2024: B; MSCI ESG: A; FT Europe Climate Leaders (2021–2024); Moody’s V.E: 52/100.

- Reporting basis (CSRD/ESRS):
  - First year reporting under CSRD framework; phase-in exemptions applied for certain indicators (to be reported by 2025/2027 per regulation).
  - Limited year-on-year comparatives due to the new framework; no material information withheld for sensitivity reasons.
  - Consolidated reporting scope aligned with financial statements across the Caixa Group (commercial banking, asset management, investment banking, venture capital), excluding low-materiality real estate holding entities.

structure.title: Sustainability Statement
structure.heading: 4.4 Sustainability Statement
structure.start_phrase:
The Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) aims to ensure that companies disclose 
sustai nability information that is reliable, comparable, and relevant for stakeholders to assess the non -
financial performance of companies.
structure.summary:
- Reports on sustainable finance efforts, including publication of the second Allocation and Impact Report for sustainable debt in 2024 and information on projects financed.
- Aligns climate-related disclosures with TCFD to provide clear, consistent reporting on climate risks and impacts.
- Demonstrates ESG performance through external ratings and indices: steady improvement in Sustainalytics’ ESG Risk Rating from 2021–2025 (reaching 13.4 in 2025, placing CGD among the top 10% of banks), CDP Climate Change 2024 score B (02/2025), MSCI ESG Rating A (06/2024), inclusion in the Financial Times Europe Climate Leaders 2024 (also 2021–2023), and Moody’s V.E 52/100 (01/2024).
- Explains the basis of preparation under the CSRD/ESRS: first year reporting under the new framework (not yet transposed nationally), limited year-on-year comparability for most indicators, and no material changes beyond those stemming from CSRD/ESRS implementation.
- Uses CSRD phase-in exemptions, with some indicators deferred to 2025 and 2027; where ESRS lacks specific standards for material topics, discloses own indicators or uses GRI.
- Addresses confidentiality: acknowledges right to withhold sensitive information but reports that no such withholding was necessary; no exemptions used for imminent facts or ongoing negotiations.
- Defines reporting scope: consolidated Caixa Group (Commercial Banking, Asset Management, Investment Banking, Venture Capital); excludes specific disclosures for low-materiality entities (Caixa Imobiliário, Imobiliária Caixa Geral, Imobci, and Caixa Participações, SGPS); overall consolidation aligned with the financial statements except for these noted entities.

nodes.title: General disclosures
nodes.heading: 4.4.1 General disclosures
nodes.start_phrase:
The Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) aims to ensure that companies disclose 
sustai nability information that is reliable, comparable, and relevant for stakeholders to assess the non -
financial performance of companies.
nodes.summary:
- ESG reporting and performance: Published 2024 Allocation and Impact Report for sustainable debt; aligned disclosures with TCFD; notable improvement in ESG ratings (Sustainalytics from 21.3 in 2021 to 13.4 in 2025; MSCI ESG Rating A; CDP Climate Change B; inclusion in FT Europe Climate Leaders; Moody’s V.E 52/100).
- Basis of preparation under CSRD/ESRS: First year applying CSRD; phase-in and comparatives largely not provided; consolidated group scope (commercial banking, asset management, investment banking, venture capital); methodology updates to Scope 3 (added category 15 for group entities; ceased reporting categories 5 and 6); information aligned with supervisory expectations and UTAM requirements; use of GRI/own indicators where ESRS not specific; no external validation beyond assurance provider; selective disclosure exemptions considered but not used.
- Strategy and alignment: Sustainability embedded as a core strategic vector in 2021–2024 plan; five sustainability action areas (financing, climate risk, inclusion, governance, disclosure); target of €1.5bn cumulative ESG financing in Portugal; commitment to enhance reporting quality in 2025–2028 cycle.
- Business model and value chain: Universal bank leadership in Portugal; strong 2024 performance (net income €1.735bn; turnover €165bn), growth in loans/deposits, market leadership in several lines; expanding digital/mobile customers; ESG-linked products and preferential pricing; broad international footprint; clear upstream (investors, suppliers) and downstream (customers, communities) value chain mapping; Sustainability Committee with cross-functional participation.
- Double materiality process: Structured CSRD/ESRS 2-aligned approach; defined time horizons; extensive stakeholder engagement (14 groups, 2,301 survey responses plus interviews); internal expert input; evaluation using severity/probability/magnitude/irreversibility and heat maps; periodic review plan and integration into strategy and risk models.
- Material topics and ESRS scope: Material per ESRS E1, S1, S3, S4, G1; topics include climate change, community support, human resources management, customer relations, digital transformation and innovation, corporate governance, ethics/conduct/compliance, sustainable financing and investment, risk management, privacy/data protection. ESRS E2–E5 and S2 deemed not material.
- Material impacts, risks, and opportunities:
  - Impacts: Negative—portfolio and value chain GHG emissions; Positive—talent attraction/retention, community development, responsible marketing, ESG financing/investment.
  - Risks: Physical and transition climate risks (including failure to meet GHG targets), HR turnover/talent shortages, evolving compliance risks.
  - Opportunities: Portfolio decarbonisation; HR development/wellbeing; responsible product alignment; digital/AI to enhance efficiency and CX; stronger ESG disclosure; new ESG products; integrating ESG in risk models; enhanced privacy/data protection.
- Due diligence and controls: ESRS-mapped due diligence activities (governance integration, stakeholder dialogue, impact assessment, mitigation, monitoring/communication); sustainability reporting risks and controls being formalized and embedded via the Sustainability Committee.
- Governance for sustainability: State-owned public limited company with Anglo-Saxon model (Board, Executive Committee, Audit Committee, SROC); Governance and Risk Committees overseeing sustainability and climate/environmental risks; CRO accountable for ESG risks; Corporate Support Department leading strategy and coordination across entities; local Sustainability Officers; strong board diversity, suitability, and training programs; Sustainability Committee (chaired by CEO) supervises strategy execution and climate/finance initiatives.
- Remuneration and ESG: Executive variable pay tied to multi-dimensional KPIs including ESG; Employee Remuneration Policy embeds sustainability, risk appetite, non-discrimination, and anti–mis-selling principles; Balanced Scorecard includes corporate ESG KPI (12.5% weight) based on Sustainalytics, CDP, MSCI; variable pay deferred over 5 years via instruments; commercial incentives aligned with risk appetite.
- Stakeholder engagement: Ongoing multi-channel engagement with customers, employees, investors, regulators, suppliers, and community; 2024 double materiality consultation integrated into governance decisions and next strategic cycle.
- Climate change (ESRS E1): Climate integrated into strategy and prudential risk categories; identified negative impact (portfolio GHGs), key risks (physical, failure to meet targets, transition), and opportunity (portfolio decarbonisation); alignment with ECB climate/environmental risk expectations and EBA ESG risk guidelines.

nodes.title: Environmental information
nodes.heading: 4.4.2 Environmental information
nodes.start_phrase: As a leading financial institution in Portugal, Caixa has robustly integrated climate challenges into its overall strategy and risk management model, in response to the expectations of the supervisor and regulator in these matters.
nodes.summary:
- Climate change integration: Caixa embeds climate considerations into strategy, governance, and risk management, aligning with ECB/EBA expectations and EU/Portugal decarbonization goals. Climate risks are treated as cross-cutting drivers of traditional prudential risks.

- Double materiality IROs: Identifies negative impacts from portfolio GHG emissions; risks from physical and transition drivers and potential target shortfalls; and opportunities via portfolio decarbonization.

- Policies and governance: Adoption of Climate & Environmental Risk Management Policy, Sustainability Policy, a 2050 Carbon Neutrality Transition Plan, and an Environmental Management System (EMS) governance model. Group-wide action plan to meet ECB’s 13 expectations and EBA ESG risk guidelines.

- Risk assessment and scenarios: Annual climate/environmental materiality assessment using short-, medium-, and long-term horizons; BES scan of macro, regulatory, tech, social, and geopolitical trends; NGFS scenario use—Net-Zero 2050 as central for transition risks, Current Policies for physical risks, with sensitivity to Delayed Transition.

- Transition plan and targets: NZBA commitment to net-zero by 2050; SBTi-based 2030 targets for own operations (Scope 1+2: -42% vs 2021) and priority sectors (electricity generation, commercial real estate, cement). Pillar III prudential targets set for 2026 and distances to IEA NZE 2050 2030 goals across electricity, fossil fuels, cement, and aviation.

- Implementation and monitoring: Climate strategy monitoring manual with KPIs/KRIs; no use of carbon credits or internal carbon pricing. 2024 progress reported by sector (e.g., significant intensity reductions in electricity generation project finance and commercial real estate; mixed results in corporate electricity and cement).

- Financed emissions accounting: First full Scope 3 estimate across 15 categories shows 99.5% in category 15 (investments). PCAF-based financed emissions calculated by sector for Portugal and other entities; 36% primary data quality.

- Environmental management and operations: 10 years EMS certification at HQ; new HQ under construction targeting BREEAM Excellent and Passive House (considering LEED/WELL for fit-out), with projected energy use/emission reductions. €122m invested in 2024 and €118m planned for sustainability-related capex. Asset management ESG initiatives (NZAM, Climate Action 100+) and launch of Caixa ESG Awards. Subsidiaries implement solar PV and fleet electrification.

- EU Taxonomy disclosures: Methodology for eligibility/alignment across counterparties and households; constraints due to data availability; application of DNSH through risk practices. Reported GAR of 4.0%, with households (mortgages/vehicles) the main contributor; improvement vs 2023 driven by better corporate data coverage and refined mortgage analysis. Ongoing plans to enhance ESG data collection and expand taxonomy-aligned products (e.g., Caixa ESG Credit Line).

- Social information – own workforce (ESRS S1): HR management anchored in respect, equity, inclusion, and well-being. IROs highlight job creation benefits, turnover risk, and opportunities in talent attraction/retention, career development, and psychosocial support. Key policies include Recruitment & Selection, Mobility, and Training & Talent Development, with a 2024 Training Plan aligned to strategic skills and regulatory requirements.

nodes.title: Social information
nodes.heading: 4.4.3 Social information
nodes.start_phrase: For Caixa, the existence of a management system focused on human resources and on a responsible leadership should involve all of the company's hierarchical levels, promoting the creation of an environment of respect, equity and inclusion, allowing the deve lopment and well -being of its employees.
nodes.summary:
- Scope of the excerpt: Social information covering ESRS S1 (Own workforce), ESRS S3 (Affected communities), ESRS S4 (Consumers and end-users), and the opening of ESRS G1 (Business conduct/Corporate Governance).

- Human Resources Management (ESRS S1):
  - Double materiality IROs: positive job creation; risk of high turnover; opportunities in talent attraction/retention, career development, psychosocial support, and work-life balance.
  - Policies: Recruitment & Selection (merit-based, global scope), Mobility (as a retention and development lever), Training Plan 2024, Training & Talent Development Policy, BNU Macau Career Path, Work Organisation Model (in-person/hybrid/telework), Equality Plan and DEI Policy, Human Rights Commitment, Anti-harassment Code. Executive Committee oversees implementation.
  - Talent attraction initiatives and results: Geração Caixa internship (5,415 applicants; 172 trainees in 2024; 374 hires since inception), expanded Mentoring to all new or newly appointed staff, university Open Days (250 students), Summer Academy (42 interns), job fairs and career days in PT/Macau.
  - Talent retention: Merit & Excellence Awards (337 total awardees; 60 in 2025 edition), robust internal mobility (2017–2024 avg. 18%; 2024: 1,181 moves, 19% rate).
  - Training and development: €3.7m invested in 2024 (+26% YoY); structured onboarding (“100% Caixa”), Talent Management (6,378 hours for High Flyers/Top Performers), support for Executive MBAs (54 employees, rising), Learning Hub (lifelong learning incl. ESG, health), leadership programmes (8,500 hours), “Upgrade” for front line (1,437 participants; 35,000 hours), 75% staff with at least one international certification, Board PEP on ESG, GenAI pilot planned for 2025, BNU Macau delivered 20,614 hours.
  - 1st Group Sustainability Week: alignment and capacity building across 8 geographies; 545 participants; 2,800 training hours; streamed to 8 countries.
  - Occupational health, wellbeing, and work-life balance: Employee Support Programme (575 supported), Health & Wellbeing partnerships, birthday leave, telework support for parents/caregivers, hybrid work (14% uptake), socially focused mobility, Life Balance talks, corporate volunteering, extra vacation day (55+ with 30Y service), extended maternity leave at BNU Macau (to 90 days), Healthy Enterprise participation.
  - DEI: four pillars (equality/equity, culture/diversity, generations/knowledge, inclusion); risks managed via communication/training, on-the-job knowledge sharing, equitable career management; Equality Plan updated annually (2025 edition live); maturity index 92% (+2pp), with progress on women’s promotions, zero harassment cases, and health/wellbeing initiatives; 2025 priorities: more women in management, deeper internal DEI literacy, family–work reconciliation, and external visibility.
  - Targets/metrics: active monitoring via Sustainability Committee; training investment disclosed; 2025–2028 HR targets to be set.

- Community Support (ESRS S3):
  - Strategy and governance: material positive impact through social/environmental/economic development of communities; embedded in Sustainability Strategy pillars; Sustainability Committee (quarterly) monitors; policies include Sustainability Policy (support to communities; alignment with PRB, NZBA, WEPs, UNGC, SDGs, etc.) and Corporate Volunteering Policy; Human Rights Commitment statement.
  - Third-sector support: Caixa Social Awards (2024: 44 projects; €1,006,630; 365 apps; nationwide; cumulative since 2019: 180 projects; >€3.7m); volunteer evaluators; impact reporting; award ceremony.
  - Corporate Volunteering: 827 employee volunteers; >2,254 hours; >47 institutions; Week of Active Citizenship; Group-wide action on International Volunteering Day.
  - Goods Donation Programme: 2,098 furniture items and 271 IT units donated to >48 institutions.
  - Group Christmas Campaign: €281,583 donated to 43 institutions; volunteer actions across six geographies; collections, blood drives, solidarity events.
  - Education initiatives: Caixa IU Programme (€10.1m to 120+ HEIs; tailored banking and 360+ prizes/grants); Caixa Mais Mundo Awards (€600k; 480 awards/scholarships in 2024; six editions: 1,410 students; €1.6m total); EPIS scholarships and youth inclusion projects; BNU Macau scholarships and training support; BCI’s support to Girl Move Academy (women’s leadership in Mozambique).
  - Vulnerable citizens: “Sou Cidadão” IDs for homeless (2024: 106; since 2019: 397; €15,365); Caixa Blood Donor Group (14,929 registered; 3,167 successful donations supporting ~9,501 patients; activity up vs. 2023); refugee student support (APGES: two master’s scholarships; Nexus: two Afghan MBA students); Timor “Natal ba Povu” (gifts and supplies for children).
  - Culture: Culturgest (115,000 in-person; >140,000 online; accessible pricing; EU projects Common Stories and Europe Beyond Access II; improved physical accessibility); Caixa Cultura Programme (7 projects; €100,000); Caixa Alfama Festival; Caixa Fado Festival in Angola.
  - Targets/metrics: 2021–2024 community investment target €40m; achieved €59.9m total (2024: €18.9m); diverse project-level KPIs; new 2025–2028 targets in development.

- Customer Relations (ESRS S4):
  - Material topics: positive impact from responsible marketing/sales (informed decisions); opportunity to keep adapting offer to needs; attention to data privacy, clear information, and financial literacy.
  - Governance and policies: Executive Board for Products oversees launches, compliance, and feedback; Product Governance & Approval Policy; Customer Complaints & Suggestions regulation; Quality Policy; Human Rights commitment referenced.
  - Customer experience and service improvements (2024 capex €17.6m): integrated CX/complaints/process quality under one area; new in-branch service system; migration to virtual tellers; instant debit card issuance and PIN recovery via digital; sensitive-process alerts; streamlined heirs certification, data updates, account closure, mortgage renegotiations; enhanced corporate lending platform and systems; stronger contact centre; bolstered fraud prevention.
  - Group initiatives: BNU Macau launched Google Pay; 69% rate service as excellent/good; BNU Timor launched a full-service mobile branch (BNU Móvel) to expand access; Banco Comercial do Atlântico deployed “Nha Bex” remote ticketing to cut wait times.
  - Market offer oversight: 66 products approved in 2024; Sustainability team consults to mitigate greenwashing; monthly tactical review of offer vs. regulation, competitors, and feedback; no identified customer harm events due to product/service features.
  - Financial literacy: Saldo Positivo portal (6m visits; 8.6m views; ~500k monthly visitors; 27–30 articles/month; 136k Facebook followers) covering ESG, budgeting, taxation, digital topics, and more.
  - Complaints management: ISO 9001-certified process; strong monitoring/reporting; Dec-2024 complaints volume 31% lower YoY; average response time under 4 working days; top issues: service (9%), fraud (5%), heirs certification (5%); process reorganisation and automation addressed pain points; BNU Macau complaints down ~6% with behavioural training.
  - Ongoing engagement: “Encontros Fora da Caixa” monthly events engage regional business and stakeholders.

- Governance (ESRS G1 – opening):
  - Emphasises the importance of a robust governance model for transparency, ESG integration across the organisation, effective disclosure, and stakeholder engagement.

nodes.title: Governance information
nodes.heading: 4.4.4 Governance information
nodes.start_phrase: In the financial sector, the existence of a robust governance model plays a key role in promoting transparency, especially with regard to the cross -cutting integration of the ESG strategic vision within the Bank and the respective disclosure of its perform ance to stakeholders.
nodes.summary:
- Customer focus and metrics:
  - Monitoring of complaints, customer experience, and satisfaction to guide improvements.
  - 2024 closed with 31% fewer complaints versus 2023 and positive evolution in customer experience metrics.
  - 2025–2028 Sustainability Strategic Plan will define corporate customer‑relations targets and metrics.
  - Continuous improvement via suggestion intake, top‑management reviews, and CO‑Complaints’ support for website FAQs, safety guidance, and multi‑channel contact (information requests, complaints, suggestions, compliments).

- Corporate governance for ESG reporting (ESRS G1 – Business conduct):
  - Emphasis on robust governance to ensure transparent, accurate, and stakeholder‑aligned ESG disclosure.
  - Double materiality analysis identified the opportunity to disclose ESG information aligned with best practices/benchmarks.
  - ESG embedded in strategic pillars (2021–2024 Strategic Plan and Sustainability Strategy).
  - Governance overseen by the Sustainability Committee (chaired by the CEO; meets at least quarterly).
  - Reporting frameworks: continued use of GRI and TCFD; began reporting under ESRS in 2024 to align with CSRD.

- Policies and internal regulations underpinning ESG disclosure:
  - Code of Conduct (truthful, clear, objective information as a core value).
  - Sustainability Policy (responsible communication and compliance).
  - Internal Regulation on the Management Report and Accounts (transparent non‑financial disclosure enabling peer comparison).
  - Internal Corporate Regulation on Executive Boards and Committees (formalizes the Sustainability Committee’s role).

- 2024 actions and oversight:
  - Board/committee supervision of ESG performance and non‑financial reporting.
  - Approvals/publications: 2023 Management Report and Accounts; updated TCFD report; sustainable debt Allocation & Impact Report; Social Impact Assessment for Caixa Social Awards; CSRD adaptation and IRO approval.
  - Identified reporting challenges: ESRS data collection strengthening, regulatory coexistence/timing, and CSRD familiarity across geographies; development of support tools and controls.
  - Alignment with supervisor expectations (ECB, Bank of Portugal, EBA), including Market Discipline (Pillar 3) disclosures and response to ECB climate/environmental risk guidance.

International network launched green/ESG products (Angola ESG car leasing; BNU Macau Eco-Car; Mozambique Eco-Environmental line; Cape Verde renewable energy credit; Timor green lines; France green loans).

Key policies: Risk Appetite, Risk Taxonomy, C&E Risk Policy, Credit Risk Policy, Healthy Origination Guidelines, Exclusion Principles.
